name: Charles Oliveira
milestone_by_age_26: Made UFC debut in August 2010 at age 20, winning by submission in 41 seconds; already held a 12-0 professional MMA record and multiple BJJ championship titles.
early_history_summary: Born in a favela in Guarujá, Brazil, Oliveira started Brazilian jiu-jitsu at age 12 and quickly won multiple regional and national BJJ titles, including the CBJJE World Championship in 2007 as a blue belt. He transitioned to professional MMA in 2008, winning three fights in one night in a tournament, and compiled a 12-0 record before signing with the UFC at age 20.
family_context_summary: Born into humble origins in the favela of Vicente de Carvalho in Guarujá, São Paulo, Brazil; parents were of modest means and his father also trained in BJJ alongside him.
primary_early_advantage_tags: favela origin,early BJJ specialization,heart condition adversity,submission expertise
evidence_summary: Oliveira grew up in a Brazilian favela and overcame a childhood heart condition diagnosis to begin BJJ at age 12, rapidly accumulating championship titles. By 18 he was a CBJJE World Champion and transitioned to pro MMA, winning three fights in one night. He signed with the UFC at 20 and won his debut by submission in 41 seconds. His path was driven by early specialization in BJJ, dedicated coaching from Ericson Cardoso, and the adversity of his background creating urgency.
starting_point: Born into a poor family in the favela of Vicente de Carvalho, Guarujá, São Paulo, Brazil; father worked modest jobs and mother initially opposed fighting.
current_position: Former UFC Lightweight Champion and current UFC BMF titleholder; ranked #3 in UFC lightweight rankings as of 2026; holds UFC records for most submissions (17), most finishes (21), and most bonuses (21).

trajectory.event: Won CBJJE World Championship as a blue belt in Brazilian jiu-jitsu.

Made UFC debut, defeating Darren Elkins by submission in 41 seconds.
Won the UFC Lightweight Championship by defeating Michael Chandler via TKO.

Won the symbolic UFC BMF Championship.

name: Carry Geijssen
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the 1000m at the 1968 Winter Olympics in Grenoble, becoming the first Dutch Olympic champion in speed skating history; also won Olympic silver in the 1500m.
early_history_summary: Geijssen emerged as a competitive speed skater in the Netherlands in the mid-1960s, winning silver at the Dutch Allround Championships in 1965 at age 18 and becoming Dutch Allround Champion in 1966 at age 19. She won bronze at the 1968 World Allround Championships before her Olympic triumph.
family_context_summary: Born in Amsterdam, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Dutch speed skating ecosystem,national championship,early competition
evidence_summary: Geijssen was part of the strong Dutch speed skating tradition, winning national championship medals starting at age 18 in 1965. She became Dutch Allround Champion at 19 in 1966 and won World Championship bronze at 21 before her Olympic gold. The Netherlands was an emerging frontier for speed skating, and she benefited from the national training infrastructure and coaching. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Amsterdam, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from competitive speed skating; later lived in Indonesia and Canada; first Dutch Olympic champion in speed skating history.

trajectory.event: Won silver at the Dutch Allround Championships.

name: Martinus J. G. Veltman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; received MSc in 1956 at age 25 but was then drafted into military service. His major achievements (PhD 1963, Schoonschip computer algebra system, renormalization of Yang-Mills theory, Nobel Prize 1999) all came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Veltman started studying mathematics and physics at Utrecht University in 1948 at age 17, received his MSc in 1956 at age 25, and was then drafted into military service for two years. His doctoral research began in 1959 and his PhD was awarded in 1963 at age 32.
family_context_summary: Born in Waalwijk, Netherlands; father was head of the local primary school and several of his father's siblings were primary school teachers; mother's father was a contractor and ran a café.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was head of the local primary school; family had an educational background but not in physics specifically.
evidence_summary: Veltman came from an educated family in the Netherlands (father was a school headmaster) and started university at 17. He had an early interest in radio electronics. However, his MSc at age 25 was standard academic progression, and his major scientific contributions came well after age 26, with his PhD in 1963, the Schoonschip computer algebra system in 1963-64, and the Nobel Prize-winning renormalization work in 1971.

name: Buzz Aldrin
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated third in his class from the United States Military Academy at West Point in 1951 at age 21, then flew 66 combat missions in the Korean War as an F-86 fighter pilot, shooting down two MiG-15 aircraft by age 23.
early_history_summary: Aldrin grew up in Montclair, New Jersey, the son of an Army aviator and Standard Oil executive. He entered West Point in 1947, finished first in his class his plebe year, and graduated third overall in 1951 with a BS in mechanical engineering. He then chose the Air Force and became a fighter pilot in Korea.
family_context_summary: Born in Glen Ridge, New Jersey; father was an Army aviator in WWI, assistant commandant of the Army's test pilot school, and later an executive at Standard Oil; family was upper-middle class.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a career Army aviator and test pilot school official, providing direct military aviation domain exposure and networks; father secured a senatorial appointment to a service academy for Aldrin.
primary_early_advantage_tags: military family,West Point,senatorial appointment,Standard Oil executive father
evidence_summary: Aldrin benefited from a privileged background: his father was an Army aviator turned Standard Oil executive who secured a senatorial appointment to a service academy. Aldrin entered West Point in 1947, excelled academically (3rd in class of 1951), and became a decorated fighter pilot in Korea with two confirmed MiG kills. His father's military aviation domain expertise and networks directly catalyzed his early career path. The elite institutional pipeline of West Point concentrated opportunity and positioned him for his later astronaut career.
starting_point: Born to an upper-middle-class family in Glen Ridge, New Jersey; father was a former Army aviator and Standard Oil executive who had been assistant commandant of the Army's test pilot school.
current_position: Retired astronaut and advocate for Mars exploration; living in the United States; second person to walk on the Moon during Apollo 11 in 1969.

trajectory.event: Graduated third in his class from the United States Military Academy at West Point with a BS in mechanical engineering.

Became the second person to walk on the Moon as part of the Apollo 11 mission.

name: Ding Liren
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Chinese Chess Championship in 2009 at age 16, becoming the youngest Chinese chess champion in history, and earned the grandmaster title the same year.
early_history_summary: Ding was born in Wenzhou, China, a city declared 'The City of Chess' after a 1995 match by Viktor Korchnoi. He started learning chess at age 4 and was enrolled in the local chess club at age 6, becoming a pupil of legendary coach Chen Lixing. He won his age group in the Li Chengzhi Cup multiple times and tied for first at the U-10 and U-12 World Youth Championships in 2003 and 2004.
family_context_summary: Born in Wenzhou, Zhejiang, China; parents enrolled him in the local chess club at age 6 after the city was declared 'The City of Chess'; family background otherwise not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond parents enrolling him in chess club.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Wenzhou chess city,Chen Lixing coaching,early tournament success,prodigy
evidence_summary: Ding grew up in Wenzhou, a city designated 'The City of Chess' after a 1995 high-profile match, and was enrolled in the local chess club at age 6. He studied under legendary coach Chen Lixing, who had mentored multiple Chinese chess prodigies. Ding won his age group in the Li Chengzhi Cup many times and tied for first at the U-10 and U-12 World Youth Championships. At 16, he won the Chinese Chess Championship as an untitled player, becoming the youngest champion ever and earning his grandmaster title. His early trajectory was driven by the Wenzhou chess ecosystem, elite coaching, and prodigy-level talent.
starting_point: Born in Wenzhou, Zhejiang, China; parents enrolled him in the local chess club at age 6 after the city was designated 'The City of Chess.'
current_position: 17th FIDE World Chess Champion (2023-2024); currently ranked #15 in the world with a rating of 2738 as of July 2026.

name: Tatiana Gutsu
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Olympic all-around gold medal at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at age 16, along with team gold, silver on uneven bars, and bronze on floor exercise.
early_history_summary: Gutsu started gymnastics at age 6 in Odesa, Ukraine, and became a member of the Soviet Union national team in 1988 at age 12. She won team gold and two silver medals at the 1991 World Championships at age 15, then won the all-around, vault, and balance beam titles at the 1992 European Championships before her Olympic triumph.
family_context_summary: Born into a Ukrainian family with Moldovan roots in Odesa, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union; family background otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet gymnastics pipeline,national team age 12,renowned coaches,prodigy difficulty
evidence_summary: Gutsu was a prodigy who started gymnastics at 6 in Odesa and was recruited to the Soviet national team at age 12, benefiting from the elite Soviet gymnastics pipeline with its renowned coaches and facilities. She was noted for performing some of the most difficult routines in the sport, including a double-twisting Yurchenko vault and a double layout somersault on floor. By 15 she was winning World Championship medals, and at 16 she became Olympic all-around champion. Her trajectory was driven by physical talent, early specialization, and the concentrated Soviet gymnastics ecosystem.
starting_point: Born into a Ukrainian family with Moldovan roots in Odesa, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union; family background otherwise not documented.
current_position: Retired from gymnastics after the 1992 Olympics due to injuries; later moved to the United States, settled in Ohio, and coached gymnastics; inducted into the International Gymnastics Hall of Fame in 2022.

trajectory.event: Became a member of the Soviet Union national gymnastics team.
Won team gold and two silver medals at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Indianapolis.
Won Olympic all-around gold, team gold, silver on uneven bars, and bronze on floor at the Barcelona Olympics.
Won all-around, vault, and balance beam titles at the European Championships.

He served as vice president of the university (1988-1991) and headmaster (1990-1993) before becoming mayor of Bogotá in 1995.
family_context_summary: Born in Bogotá, Colombia; family background not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Hu Shuli
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; she was still an undergraduate at Renmin University when she turned 26, having entered in 1978 and graduated in 1982. Her notable achievements (founding Caijing in 1998, Caixin Media in 2010) came well after age 26.
early_history_summary: Hu Shuli was born in Beijing to a family with deep journalism and publishing roots. She attended the prestigious 101 Middle School and entered Renmin University of China in 1978 when college classes resumed, graduating in journalism in 1982 at age 29. She worked at Worker's Daily before founding Caijing magazine in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born in Beijing; grandfather was a translator and editor at Shen Bao, great-uncle Hu Yuzhi was an early proponent of language reform and publishing, mother was a senior editor at Workers' Daily, father had a midlevel post in a trade union.
parent_family_domain_summary: Strong journalism and publishing lineage: grandfather was a translator/editor, great-uncle was a prominent publisher and literary figure, mother was a senior editor at Workers' Daily.

evidence_summary: Hu Shuli came from a prominent journalism and publishing family in Beijing — her grandfather was a translator/editor, her great-uncle was a noted publisher, and her mother was a senior editor. However, due to the Cultural Revolution disruption of Chinese higher education, she did not enter university until 1978 at age 25, graduating at 29. Her notable career achievements came decades later. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Lars-Eric Lundvall
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Swedish national hockey championship with Södertälje SK in 1956 at age 22, and was a World Champion with Sweden at the 1957 World Championships at age 23; debuted for the Swedish national team in 1954 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Lundvall started playing hockey with IFK Bofors in Karlskoga, Sweden, and made his debut for the Swedish national team (Tre Kronor) in autumn 1954 at age 20. He moved to Södertälje SK in 1955 and won the Swedish title with them in 1956. He won World Championship gold with Sweden in 1957 and again in 1962.
family_context_summary: Born in Karlskoga, Sweden; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond having a brother Jan-Olof Lundvall.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish hockey pipeline,national team debut at 20,club system
evidence_summary: Lundvall emerged from the Swedish ice hockey club system, starting with IFK Bofors in Karlskoga before moving to Södertälje SK. He debuted for the Swedish national team at 20 and won the Swedish championship at 22 and World Championship gold at 23. He formed a key partnership with teammate Ronald Pettersson in both club and national team. The Swedish hockey pipeline provided the institutional structure for his development, though family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Karlskoga, Sweden; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on April 8, 2020, at age 86 in Gothenburg, Sweden; final role was ice hockey coach with Västra Frölunda IF and gas station owner.

name: Douglas Adams
milestone_by_age_26: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy radio series first broadcast on BBC Radio 4 on 8 March 1978, when Adams was 25 (three days before his 26th birthday), launching the franchise that made him famous.
early_history_summary: Adams grew up in Essex, England, and attended Brentwood School before entering St John's College, Cambridge in 1971, where he joined the Footlights comedy club. After graduating in 1974, he wrote briefly with Graham Chapman for Monty Python's Flying Circus, then struggled for several years before pitching The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy to BBC Radio 4 in 1977.
family_context_summary: Born in Cambridge to Christopher Douglas Adams, a management consultant and computer salesman who formerly worked as a probation officer, and Janet Dora Sydney Adams, a nurse; parents divorced when he was five; raised by his mother in Essex.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a management consultant and computer salesman; paternal grandfather came from a long line of distinguished doctors; no direct writing or comedy family background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cambridge Footlights,Brentwood School,John Cleese mentorship,Graham Chapman collaboration
evidence_summary: Adams attended Brentwood School in Essex where a form master recognized his creative writing talent, then won an exhibition to St John's College, Cambridge, where he joined the Footlights comedy club in 1972. The Footlights network connected him with future collaborators and gave him access to the Cambridge comedy ecosystem. After graduating in 1974, his brief writing partnership with Graham Chapman of Monty Python gave him a writing credit on the show. His Cambridge peers (Simon Jones, Geoffrey McGivern, John Lloyd) became key collaborators on Hitchhiker's Guide. The institutional pipeline of Cambridge and Footlights was central to his early career.
starting_point: Born in Cambridge, England to a management consultant father and nurse mother; parents divorced when he was five; raised by his mother in Essex in modest circumstances.
current_position: Died on 11 May 2001 at age 49 in Santa Barbara, California; final role was author and digital media entrepreneur; best known for The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy series.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Cambridge and received a writing credit on Monty Python's Flying Circus through collaboration with Graham Chapman.

name: Dua Lipa
milestone_by_age_26: Released her self-titled debut album in 2017 at age 21, which spawned the UK number-one single 'New Rules'; won Grammy Awards for Best New Artist and Best Dance Recording in 2019 at age 23; released Future Nostalgia in 2020 and won Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album in 2021 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in London to Kosovo Albanian parents, Lipa was influenced by her father, a rock musician. She returned to London alone at 15, attended Sylvia Young Theatre School, posted covers on YouTube, worked as a model, and signed with Warner Bros. Records in 2014. Her debut album in 2017 launched her to stardom with multiple hit singles.
family_context_summary: Born in London to Kosovo Albanian parents; father Dukagjin Lipa was a rock singer and guitarist in the Kosovan band Oda who later became a marketing executive; mother Anesa (née Rexha); both grandfathers were historians; family returned to Kosovo when she was 11.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a musician (lead singer/guitarist of Kosovan rock band Oda) who influenced her musically from childhood, playing music at home and exposing her to diverse artists; both grandfathers were historians.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YouTube covers,Sylvia Young Theatre School,father musician,Warner Bros signing,social media
evidence_summary: Dua Lipa grew up in a musical household — her father was a rock musician in Kosovo — which gave her early musical exposure. She strategically used YouTube and SoundCloud as a teenager to build an audience, posting covers that attracted industry attention. She attended the prestigious Sylvia Young Theatre School, worked as a model to make industry contacts, and signed with Warner Bros. Records in 2014 at age 18-19. Her online platform presence was a repeatable distribution channel that directly led to her signing. She also benefited from the management team behind Lana Del Rey. Her trajectory exemplifies platform-native compounding through social media and streaming.
starting_point: Born in London to Kosovo Albanian parents; father was a rock musician turned marketing executive, mother raised the family; grew up in West Hampstead before moving to Kosovo at age 11 and returning to London at 15.
current_position: Global pop superstar with three Grammy Awards and seven Brit Awards; released third album Radical Optimism in 2024; married actor Callum Turner in 2026; net worth estimated in the tens of millions.

name: Maria Sharapova
milestone_by_age_26: Won Wimbledon at age 17 in 2004, became world No. 1 at age 18 in 2005, won the US Open in 2006 at age 19, and the Australian Open in 2008 at age 20; by age 26 she held three Grand Slam titles and had been ranked No. 1 multiple times.
early_history_summary: Sharapova started tennis at age 4 in Sochi, Russia, and moved to Florida at age 7 with her father to train at the IMG/Bollettieri Academy. She turned professional at 14, won the Eddie Herr Junior title at 13, reached junior Grand Slam finals at 14, and won her first WTA title at 16 before her Wimbledon breakthrough at 17.
family_context_summary: Born in Nyagan, Russian SFSR to Yuri and Yelena Sharapov, who were from Gomel, Byelorussian SSR and left due to the Chernobyl nuclear accident; family had limited financial resources, with father borrowing money to travel to the US with $700 in savings.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Yuri befriended Aleksandr Kafelnikov (father of future tennis star Yevgeny Kafelnikov) who gave Sharapova her first racquet; father was deeply involved in her tennis training from the start.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bollettieri/IMG Academy,early Florida move,Martina Navratilova recommendation,father sacrifice,prodigy
evidence_summary: Sharapova's father borrowed money and traveled to the US with only $700 to get her into the IMG/Bollettieri Academy in Florida, after Martina Navratilova recommended professional training at age 6. IMG paid her $35,000 annual tuition from age 9. She was a prodigy who won the Eddie Herr Junior title at 13, turned pro at 14, and won Wimbledon at 17. The elite Bollettieri pipeline, her father's network connection to the Kafelnikov family, and her extraordinary physical talent combined to create one of the most accelerated tennis careers in history. The adversity of leaving Russia with minimal resources created urgency.
starting_point: Born in Nyagan, Russian SFSR to parents who had fled the Chernobyl nuclear accident; family of modest means, father borrowed money to take her to Florida with $700 in savings.
current_position: Retired from professional tennis in 2020; inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2025; resides in Manhattan Beach, California and Bradenton, Florida; career prize money of $38.8 million.
